jobs.title: Caliche, litt over tre
jobs.scene: Scene: the sleepy one-street town of Caliche at about 03:10, population 412, on a two-lane desert highway. Ground-level establishing view looking south from the northern end of the main street. In this view west is right and east is left: on the right the small gas station then the sheriff's substation, laundromat, closed Plaza cinema with an unlettered marquee and feed store; on the left a squat concrete AM radio building with a thin mast, souvenir shop, modest church and a few low homes. Only a short low-density street, not a city and no skyline. Wooden telephone poles, sparse dusty sidewalks, amber streetlamps, one suspended yellow traffic light near the northern crossing, one or two TV-blue windows. The sheriff's office is dark because the deputy is out on patrol. Very distant low mesas and sparse starlight, no visible dawn. No crowds and no moving traffic. Let the ordinary reassuring storefronts fall gradually into unnerving darkness along the road. All signs blank, no text.
jobs.caption: Hovedgata sett sørover fra den nordlige enden. Bensinstasjonen og Plaza ligger på vestsiden, AM-stasjonen og kirken på østsiden.
jobs.status: Miljøretning for bygd gate; ingen ny kartgeometri.

jobs.title: Telefonen ved nattluka
jobs.scene: Scene: outside Caliche's modest 24-hour gas station at 03:06. A metal payphone in a shallow open-sided wall enclosure beside the night-service window is the main foreground subject, its black handset resting on the cradle, coiled metal cord, faint warm light catching the coin return with one small bright coin. Beyond the glass a tired middle-aged male attendant in a simple unbranded work shirt stands with a coffee mug; his pose is ordinary and face small, not a portrait. Dim shelves and warm tungsten inside; isolated cold fluorescent light over the window. Old squared mechanical gasoline pumps and empty dusty pavement extend into the dark, no extra people. The story beat is a phone that has begun ringing with the sound of a printer, not a visible apparition. Use framing and light to make the phone feel inexplicably important without a sound graphic. No readable text or numeric markings, no gas brand, no giant sci-fi lights.
jobs.caption: Telefonautomaten og betjenten samler det trygge og det rare på samme sted. Femcenten er liten, uten forklarende tekst i bildet.

jobs.title: Night Line, den døde linja
jobs.scene: Scene: outside the small concrete 1420 AM building in Caliche at 02:26, looking through the studio window from the dark sidewalk. In the warm glass booth a tired late-middle-aged male radio host sits sideways at a scratched desk, analog mixing console, old microphone on a simple boom, large headphones and a reel-to-reel tape machine. A black telephone sits within reach; one loose tape box rests in shadow. One small red on-air indicator is lit without lettering. His face is small and indistinct, posture intent as if listening to a caller nobody else can hear. Window reflections include a dark quiet street and the base of the thin radio mast, not a face or monster. CRT-era equipment only, no computers with flat screens. The strong compositional divide is cold empty exterior versus intimate warm studio. All equipment labels and signs are blank; do not display a real station callsign.
jobs.caption: Earl i glassburet under samtalen med gutten som sier det er juli. Den tomme gata speiler seg i vinduet.
jobs.status: Stemningskonsept ved AM-stasjonen; ingen ny innendørs spillflate.

jobs.title: Kvinnen utenfor vaskeriet
jobs.scene: Scene: a small rural Caliche laundromat at 03:20. View from across the empty sidewalk toward a worn outdoor bench under one cool fluorescent tube. A middle-aged woman in a plain old cardigan and practical slacks sits quietly on the bench holding a small 1970s transistor radio close to her lap, listening with her head slightly angled down; no smile, no theatrical fear. Her face is kept small and softly in shadow. Behind the dusty glass are a few old round-door washing machines and empty plastic chairs, the rest unlit. One amber streetlight at the edge of the composition gives a warm rim, creating a restrained warm/cool conflict. The dark end of the street and desert beyond occupy generous negative space. No other figures, no alien in the window, no visible ghosts. No text, laundry branding, contemporary equipment or rain-soaked cyberpunk pavement.
jobs.caption: Et vanlig stoppested med én som lytter mellom stasjonene. Mannens tapte 47 minutter ligger i historien, uten å illustreres som et spøkelse.
jobs.status: Miljø- og personkonsept ved eksisterende benk.

jobs.title: Bildet på motell-TV-en
jobs.scene: Scene: the small reception office of Sierra Motor Court at about 03:45. Seen from just inside the door: a worn laminate counter, a wooden cubby key rack, paper guest ledger and an unbranded black rotary telephone, all period-ordinary. A small bulky 1980s CRT television is angled toward the viewer on a shelf behind the counter. On its screen, clearly but softly rendered, is a monochrome strictly overhead view of the same little motel parking court with a single white boxy 1980s utility pickup with a service box on its bed. This is the impossible aerial camera angle from the story, not a floating object in the room. Through the office's real window the parking lot and that same pickup are seen from ground level, with a plain red motel-room door and a low peach-plaster room wing beyond. Warm amber outside and lamp light against the eerie gray CRT glow. Office empty, no people, no camera drone, no ghost, no numbers or text on screen or papers. No neon brand wording. Make the screen composition readable as an image within a physical television, not a second inset panel in the artwork.
jobs.caption: TV-en viser plassen rett ovenfra, mens samme pickup står utenfor vinduet. Hendelsen er spesifisert; bildet er et konsept for videre innbygging.
jobs.status: Konsept for spesifisert motellhendelse, ikke bevis på ferdig implementering.

jobs.title: Mellom antennene
jobs.scene: Scene: a quiet walk in the SARO radio-telescope field at about 03:00. Low human eye-level view beside a gravel service path and a large pale parabolic radio dish on its concrete pedestal. Four or five of the installation's 27 dishes are visible receding toward low flat mesas, never try to show all 27. The visible dish faces point toward the same rough northeast bearing rather than an ordered celestial laser show. An old gray service cabinet with no labels, wire fence and spare practical amber pool lights. Mostly dark navy sky with sparse fine stars, no large dramatic Milky Way painted as a nebula. One single tiny thin nonhuman silhouette stands completely still more than 70 metres away near a far pedestal at the extreme right edge, backlit only by a very faint lighter horizon. Large head, narrow body, no face, no eyes, no shine, no lit skin; barely noticeable and easy to mistake for equipment. The scene's main subject remains the ordinary imposing antenna structure and empty path, not the creature. No other figures, no spaceship, no fog column.
jobs.caption: Det store er kjent utstyr, det lille står i ytterkanten av bildet. Bare noen av anleggets 27 antenner vises.
jobs.status: Lys- og komposisjonskonsept for glimtene i antennefeltet.

jobs.title: Kabelen på STATION 01
jobs.scene: Scene: STATION 01, the abandoned modest 1947 survey site still standing in the New Mexico desert in 1986, at around 04:10 before dawn. New concept viewpoint very low beside the evidence: two severed ends of an old black field cable on dusty gravel in the foreground, exposed copper with a clean deliberate cut. A sturdy concrete transit pillar with a period mechanical optical survey transit is the central midground anchor. A tiny pale weathered stucco hut with one practical warm doorway lamp and a smaller generator shed sit off to one side, no elaborate laboratory. Three humble survey reference positions are suggested across the landscape by a few wooden stakes, weathered panels and old foundations; no luminous drawn lines or letters. An unbranded folding bellows field camera on its simple tripod is close to the cut cable, seen from behind, suggesting documentation. A shallow portable flashlight pool lets the cut ends read; the person holding it stays out of frame. Blue-black sky, low mesas, no green science fiction glow, no people or aliens, no readable labels. Emphasize observation, distance and intentional human action rather than an explosion.
sources: web/HISTORIE.md, The Survey Station og forfatterfasit
jobs.caption: Et nærmere blikk på det avkuttede kabelparet, med transitten som fast holdepunkt. Bildet bygger videre på det eksisterende stasjonskonseptet.
jobs.status: Konsept for eksisterende sted og kabelbevis; ingen ny oppmåling.

jobs.title: Roswell-veien, 05:29:47
jobs.scene: Scene: the first wider moment of the final pull-out on the old Roswell road at 05:29:47, one minute before sunrise. An isolated white boxy 1980s utility pickup with a service box on the bed has stopped aligned in its lane on a narrow worn two-lane road across a vast flat New Mexico desert. Slightly elevated rear three-quarter view, about 15 metres above and well behind the truck, looking northeast along the road toward the lightening sky. The steering compartment is dark and no occupant can be distinguished. Headlights still illuminate two quiet pools on the pavement ahead, very faint amber-green as if their color has been wrong; no flashing VFX. A modest old milepost and flush survey bolt are small at the road edge, with no readable numbers, and an ordinary wire fence follows the roadside. Horizon very pale warm peach toward the east on the right, otherwise predawn blue, almost no visible stars, the sun disk still below the horizon. Vastness and an inexplicably empty vehicle carry the ending. NO overhead beam or shaft of light, no spacecraft, no people, no alien, no ghost, no explosion, no giant cosmic portal. No title or overlay.
sources: web/KAPITLER.md, Roswell Road, kurs og uttrekk
jobs.caption: Pickupen blir liten på veien idet kameraet trekker seg ut. Gryet ligger foran og til høyre; ingen oppvåkning legges til slutten.
jobs.status: Fortellingskonsept for den vedtatte slutten; røper slutten.
